This matches the trace's ack appearing one cycle after write-strobe samples."}, {"id": "patch_f8d57d590691", "failure_port": "o_wb_ack", "source_line": 582, "mechanism": "Changes ack from `wb_stb` to `(i_wb_cyc) && (wb_stb)`. Since `wb_stb = (i_wb_stb)&&(!o_wb_stall)` and `o_wb_stall=0`, this gates ack with `i_wb_cyc` directly. The trace shows ack cycling with `i_wb_cyc`, supporting this bus-cycle qualification."}, {"id": "patch_cef2e466558e", "failure_port": "o_wb_ack", "source_line": 327, "mechanism": "Inside response-token logic, qualifies `r_have_resp` with `r_use_fifo` so `r_data_response_token` only sets when a FIFO command expects a token. Aligns command-state initialization with bus-cycle timing."}, {"id": "patch_15e507eb05d7", "failure_port": "o_wb_ack", "source_line": 305, "mechanism": "Guards state-0 to state-1 transition with `pre_cmd_state`, ensuring byte serialization only starts when bus cycle is qualified. Affects `r_cmd_busy` duration and therefore `o_wb_ack` via interrupt path."}, {"id": "patch_3466ed48d141", "failure_port": "o_wb_ack", "source_line": 324, "mechanism": "Guards state 5 entry with `!r_have_resp`, preventing transition to busy-wait before first response token. Keeps response state machine aligned with actual token arrival, indirectly stabilizing `o_wb_ack`."}], "explanation": "The trace shows `o_wb_ack` toggling every cycle starting at cycle 6 while `i_wb_cyc` also toggles, but the original code drives `o_wb_ack` directly from `wb_stb` (which follows `i_wb_stb`). Only patches `patch_a3e524527915` and `patch_f8d57d590691` modify the `o_wb_ack` assignment itself to insert a cycle delay or bus-cycle gate, directly matching the observed one-cycle-late ack pattern. The remaining patches adjust command/response state guards that indirectly influence `r_cmd_busy` and the interrupt `o_int`, which feeds back into bus behavior; they are ranked by proximity to the ack-generating logic and whether they add bus-cycle qualification seen in the trace."}
